clue.text: French writer takes on the conqueror of the Midianites

parts.note: André Gide was a French novelist and Nobel laureate
taken as written

explanation.surface: A French author takes on the role of a biblical warrior.
explanation.walkthrough: In the Book of Judges, Gideon leads Israel to defeat the Midianites; 'takes' only links the writer to ON.
explanation.definitionFit: The biblical judge Gideon routed the Midianite army with three hundred men.

clue.text: Singular example of the writing on the wall

definitions.text: Singular example of the writing on the wall

parts.words: Singular example of the writing on the wall
parts.note: scrawls on walls are known by an Italian plural word; one such scrawl takes the singular form of that word

explanation.surface: A grim omen of doom, the writing on the wall, singled out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'The writing on the wall' suggests an omen of doom, but here it is literal scrawling; 'Singular' asks for the Italian singular form.
explanation.definitionFit: Graffiti is an Italian plural; a single scribbled inscription takes the singular ending -o.

clue.text: Sweetener to upset a dreamer

indicators.note: to upset something is to knock it over, so these letters are thrown into a new order

explanation.surface: Disturbing a daydreamer just to add sugar to the tea.
explanation.walkthrough: The anagram signal 'to upset' rearranges the eight letters of A DREAMER.
explanation.definitionFit: Demerara is a coarse brown cane sugar, used to sweeten coffee and tea.

clue.text: What's-his-name runs rings round a road race

indicators.note: the rings are placed around the race, so one piece encloses the other

parts.note: two rings look like two letter Os
the TT (Tourist Trophy) is the motorcycle road race on the Isle of Man

explanation.surface: Some anonymous fellow is running laps around a road race.
explanation.walkthrough: The TT is a famous motorcycle race held on public roads on the Isle of Man; 'runs' merely links the name to its wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: Otto is a man's name, so it can stand for any unnamed fellow.

clue.text: Crazy biscuits

definitions.meaning: mad, out of one's mind, in informal speech
thin dry savoury wafers eaten with cheese

explanation.surface: Biscuits that have gone mad.
explanation.definitionFit: Informally, someone mad is said to be crackers; the word also names crisp savoury wafers.

clue.text: No sinister chap, this chief assistant

definitions.meaning: sinister is Latin for left, so a man who is not of the left side belongs to the other side
the most trusted helper of a leader

explanation.surface: The boss's main helper is no villain.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sinister' looks like 'evil', but its Latin sense is 'left', so a man not on the left is on the right side.
explanation.definitionFit: A trusted deputy is traditionally the one seated at the leader's right side; the opposite of left-handed is right-handed.

clue.text: Footwear hamper

definitions.meaning: to obstruct or block, as a verb

explanation.surface: Shoes that get in the way.
explanation.definitionFit: A clog is a wooden shoe, and to clog is to block or impede.

clue.text: Cockney kipper? It's going wrong

indicators.note: London's Cockney speech drops the H at the start of words

parts.note: a kipper is a smoked herring

explanation.surface: A Londoner's smoked fish has gone off.
explanation.walkthrough: A Cockney (an east London speaker) drops initial H, so the fish loses its first letter; 'It's' links the wordplay to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: To err is to make a mistake, so someone erring is straying from what is right.

clue.text: Said to be what naughty people pay to the Inland Revenue

definitions.text: Said to be what naughty people pay to the Inland Revenue

parts.words: Said to be what naughty people pay to the Inland Revenue
parts.note: a levy charged on wrongdoing, spoken aloud, gives the grammar word for sentence structure

explanation.surface: Wrongdoers supposedly owe a special levy to the British tax office.
explanation.walkthrough: A 'sin tax' spoken aloud sounds like the grammatical term; the Inland Revenue was the UK tax authority.
explanation.definitionFit: Syntax is the arrangement of words into sentences; spoken, it matches a levy on wickedness.

clue.text: Permits entrance, though in one way it's mad

indicators.note: taking the letters in one possible way of arranging them signals a rearrangement

parts.note: the apostrophe adds no letter

explanation.surface: A doorman lets people in, though one might call that crazy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in one way' signals that ITS and MAD can be rearranged; 'though' only links.
explanation.definitionFit: To let someone in, through a door or gate, is to allow them to enter.

clue.text: What the theatrical backer hopes to get for his money

definitions.text: What the theatrical backer hopes to get for his money

parts.words: What the theatrical backer hopes to get for his money
parts.note: an investor in a stage show wants it to play for many weeks to full houses

explanation.surface: An angel funding a play hopes for a return on the investment.
explanation.definitionFit: A long, successful series of performances is what makes a stage production profitable.

clue.text: Lingerie from the Pyrenees?

parts.note: the people of the western Pyrenees lend their name to a close-fitting women's undergarment

explanation.surface: Asking whether some underwear comes from the mountains between France and Spain.
explanation.walkthrough: A basque is a tight bodice, named after the Basque people of the Pyrenees; the question mark marks the playful geographical reading.
explanation.definitionFit: A basque is a tight-fitting top undergarment, and the Basque Country lies in the Pyrenees.

clue.text: Travel cost sounds reasonable

indicators.note: sounds signals a word that is pronounced like another

parts.note: fair means just or reasonable

explanation.surface: A ticket price that seems fair.
explanation.definitionFit: A fare is the price paid for a journey on a bus, train or taxi.

clue.text: Political high jinks

definitions.meaning: a political group, such as Labour or the Conservatives

explanation.surface: Politicians getting up to boisterous fun.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Political' stands in for a noun here: 'political ___' as in a political organisation.
explanation.definitionFit: A party is both an organised political group and a festive social gathering.

clue.text: Briefly incorporated with a Peruvian Indian

parts.note: Inc is the short form of Incorporated after a company name

explanation.surface: A company formed with a native Peruvian partner.
explanation.definitionFit: The Inca were the native people whose empire ruled Peru before the Spanish conquest.

clue.text: Light ale turns up in royal style

definitions.note: an adjective of manner: fit for or like a monarch

indicators.note: in a down clue the word is turned upwards, so it reads from bottom to top

parts.note: lager is a light beer

explanation.surface: A pale beer is served in kingly fashion.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turns up' reverses LAGER in this down entry.
explanation.definitionFit: Regal means kingly or queenly, fit for a monarch.

clue.text: Amended taxes in such a state!

indicators.note: amended means altered, so the letters are reworked

explanation.surface: Changes to taxes put people into such a fuss!
explanation.walkthrough: 'state' looks like a state of agitation, but it is a US state; 'Amended' rearranges TAXES.
explanation.definitionFit: Texas is one of the fifty United States.

clue.text: Mathematical toper's formula for one over the eight

definitions.text: Mathematical toper's formula for one over the eight

parts.words: Mathematical toper's formula for one over the eight
parts.note: a drinker's one drink too many, the ninth after eight, written as a power of a small number

explanation.surface: A drinker expresses being tipsy as a sum.
explanation.walkthrough: 'One over the eight' is British slang for slightly drunk; nine, one more than eight, is three multiplied by itself.
explanation.definitionFit: Three times three equals nine, the number one more than eight.

clue.text: A touch of nobility

parts.note: the tap of a sword on the shoulder that confers knighthood

explanation.surface: A hint of aristocratic bearing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'A touch of' suggests a small amount, but it is a literal touch: the sword tap that makes a knight.
explanation.definitionFit: An accolade was the ceremonial sword tap that dubbed a knight; it now also means praise or an award.

clue.text: In the style of superlatively good outsize fireproof stuff

parts.note: as means like or in the manner of
best is the superlative of good
OS is the clothing abbreviation for outsize

explanation.surface: Something extra-large and of the finest quality that will not burn.
explanation.definitionFit: Asbestos is a fibrous mineral formerly used to resist fire and heat.

clue.text: Lend money to assist amorous progress

definitions.meaning: to pay sums on loan before they are due
to make romantic or sexual overtures to someone

explanation.surface: A loan that helps along a courtship.
explanation.definitionFit: Advances are loans or prepayments; making them also means pursuing someone romantically.

clue.text: Add up to Tom in Oman

indicators.note: in a down entry, up means the word is read from the bottom upwards

parts.note: to sum is to add
a tom is a male cat

explanation.surface: Totalling up the cats in an Arabian country.
explanation.walkthrough: 'up' reverses SUM to MUS in this down entry; 'to' only joins it to CAT.
explanation.definitionFit: Muscat is the capital city of the Sultanate of Oman.

clue.text: Representative specimen of politician in vending event

indicators.note: the politician is placed in the middle of the sale

parts.note: a sale is an event where goods are sold
MP is a Member of Parliament

explanation.surface: A typical example of an elected member at a jumble sale.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Representative' tempts as a politician, but it is part of the definition; the politician is a British Member of Parliament.
explanation.definitionFit: A sample is a small portion taken to show what the whole is like.

clue.text: Raised like the poison tree

parts.note: up means raised or lifted
as means like

explanation.surface: Grown in the manner of a toxic tree.
explanation.definitionFit: The upas is a Javanese tree whose sap was used as arrow poison.

clue.text: Turn back on weak-minded wanderer

indicators.note: turning back the short word makes it read in reverse

parts.note: mad is used loosely for unsound in mind

explanation.surface: Rounding on a feeble-witted traveller.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Turn back on' looks like a phrase meaning abandon, but 'Turn back' reverses ON.
explanation.definitionFit: A nomad is a person with no fixed home who roams from place to place.

clue.text: Five-and-a half yards from Warsaw perhaps

definitions.meaning: an old British unit of length, also called a rod or perch
a native of Poland, whose capital is Warsaw

explanation.surface: Measuring a distance from the Polish capital.
explanation.definitionFit: A pole is an old measure of 5.5 yards; a Pole is someone from Poland.

clue.text: Caledonian type of tax

definitions.meaning: Caledonia is the Latin name for Scotland, so a Caledonian is a person from there
a historical levy, surviving in the phrase ...-free

explanation.surface: A levy imposed on Scotland.
explanation.walkthrough: To get off scot-free originally meant to escape paying this tax.
explanation.definitionFit: A Scot is a native of Scotland, and scot was a medieval municipal levy.

clue.text: Needless advice to the short-sighted nobleman

definitions.meaning: people with poor sight squint closely anyway, so telling them to look hard is pointless
a member of the House of Lords, such as a duke or earl

explanation.surface: Pointless advice given to a myopic aristocrat.
explanation.walkthrough: The first half reads the word as a command: those who see badly already look closely without being told.
explanation.definitionFit: To peer is to look hard; a peer is a British noble with a title.

clue.text: China cup broken by one of the friars

indicators.note: broken china is smashed into pieces, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Crockery shattered by a clumsy monk.
explanation.walkthrough: 'broken' rearranges the letters of CHINA CUP; 'by' only links.
explanation.definitionFit: The Capuchins are a Franciscan order of friars known for their pointed hoods.

clue.text: Renounce opinion concerning jargon

parts.note: re means about or concerning
cant is the special talk of a group

explanation.surface: Abandoning a view on specialist jargon.
explanation.definitionFit: To recant is to withdraw a belief or statement formally.

clue.text: Where play is predominant, 10 means weeks of work

definitions.text: Where play is predominant, 10 means weeks of work

parts.words: Where play is predominant, 10 means weeks of work
parts.note: venues for staged drama, where a long successful season (clue 10) keeps the company employed

explanation.surface: A place where fun dominates, but success brings weeks of labour.
explanation.walkthrough: 'play' looks like leisure, the opposite of work, but it is drama; 10 refers to A GOOD RUN, which means weeks of employment for actors.
explanation.definitionFit: These are the buildings where stage plays are performed.

clue.text: Hails cries in Scotland

explanation.surface: Weeping Scots welcome visitors.
explanation.walkthrough: In Scots dialect, to greet is to weep.
explanation.definitionFit: To greet is to welcome; in Scots dialect it means to weep.
